The rider's factual account is corroborated by the platform's own telemetry, not merely asserted.

Under POL-RD-21 the driver had to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat - or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence - before or at the point of deviation. The chat log is complete and holds only two messages, both at 11:26-11:27 and both about the taxi stand, i.e. before the 11:28:02 trip start; the trip record's messages_during_trip block is empty and in_app_calls is empty. So no chat notice was given and there is no call recording in the record, and the deviation at 11:30:14 was unannounced and unagreed. Any asserted verbal notice cannot be established under POL-RD-21 read with POL-GEN-26.

POL-RD-23 requires traffic data for the recommended segment at the trip time showing congestion, an incident or a closure. The LTA advisory for Bedok Road across the trip window (valid 10:58-12:28) reports type NONE, 'no incident, roadwork or closure', and speed bands 4-6 throughout. 'Bus stop and traffic light very long' is not one of POL-RD-23's types (closure, congestion, incident), and the driver's claim that the Siglap side is 'about the same distance' is contradicted by the recorded distances. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified, which closes the traffic-justified rows (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-24 and leaves the driver with no justification for departing the recommended route at all.

Honest concession, and the rider does not stretch the record to avoid it. POL-RD-22 makes the platform's recorded distances the measure and forbids re-measuring from the trace; on those recorded distances the deviation is 5.2 - 4.6 = 0.60 km, which is inside POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The two matrix rows that pay the excess distance fare - (b) and (d) - each require a deviation over 1 km and are therefore not available to the rider on this evidence, and the excess distance fare itself (0.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.43 SGD, not the 2.00 SGD pleaded, on POL-RD-24's formula) is not recoverable within tolerance. The rider's complaint is an unauthorised, unannounced detour, and that is the finding the record supports; the rider does not ask the tribunal to re-measure the route or to award a remedy POL-RD-24 does not provide.
